source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client refuses his oral antipsychotic, saying it is poison. He is not dangerous. The nurse should:
options: Consult the physician about a plan
questions.rationale: Medication cannot be forced unless the client is a danger; deception destroys trust. Consult on a care plan.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 205)
questions.quote: Unless the client presents a danger to himself or others, medications can't be forced on a client.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The nurse's most important initial role with a client with a mental health disorder is to:
questions.rationale: A therapeutic relationship starts with trust and rapport.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 205)
questions.quote: To establish therapeutic nurse-client relationship, it is primarily im rtant to establish trust and ra rt.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A typhoon survivor has nightmares, sleep problems and jumps at sudden noises months later. This suggests:
questions.rationale: PTSD: hyperalertness, exaggerated startle, sleep disturbance, reliving the trauma, survival guilt.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 205)
questions.quote: Signs and symptoms of post-trauma syndrome include: hyper- alertness, sleep disturbances, exaggerated startle, survival guilt

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with borderline personality disorder has fresh cuts on her wrists. The priority nursing diagnosis is:
questions.rationale: Impulsive self-destructive behavior is characteristic; safety comes first.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 205)
questions.quote: The predominant behavioral charactenstic of the client With borderline personality disorder is impulsiveness. especially of a physically self-destructive sort.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The most prominent characteristic of borderline personality disorder is:
questions.rationale: Instability in relationships, mood, behavior and self-image marks borderline PD; suspiciousness is paranoid; disregard for others is antisocial.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 209)
questions.quote: The prominent characteristic of borderline personality disorder is the patient's instability in personal relationships, mood, behavior, and self- image.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on antipsychotics for many years has involuntary tongue thrusting and lip smacking. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Tardive dyskinesia is a late effect with involuntary oral-facial and limb movements.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 205)
questions.quote: Unusual movements of the tongue, neck and arrns suggest tardlse dyskinesia.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client says, "Aliens are coming to take over the earth." The most therapeutic response is:
questions.rationale: Respond to the feeling behind the delusion without arguing or reinforcing its content.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 205)
questions.quote: This response addresses the client's underlying fears without feeding the delusion.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which drug is commonly used to detoxify clients withdrawing from opioids such as heroin?
questions.rationale: Methadone binds opioid receptors and eases withdrawal without the same harmful effects.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: Methadone is used to detoxify opiate users

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client suspected of opioid misuse would most likely show:
questions.rationale: Opioids cause euphoria, drowsiness, slurred speech and pinpoint pupils; stimulants dilate pupils.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 208)
questions.quote: Assessment findings in a patient abusing opiates include agitation. slurred h. euphoria. and constricted upils.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Drawing and puppet play with a terminally ill school-age child mainly help the child to:
questions.rationale: Children may lack words for their feelings; play offers an outlet for expression.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: Children may not have the verbal and cognitive skills to express "hat they feel and may benefit from altemative modes of expression.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client suddenly cannot see after a family crisis, with no physical cause found. The best nursing approach is to:
options: Tell him the blindness is not real
questions.rationale: In conversion disorder, attention to the symptom reinforces it and secondary gain; the symptom is real to the client; encourage self-care.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: Focustng on his blindness can positively reinforce the blindness and further promote the use of maladaptive behaviors to obtatn secondary gains.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Right after electroconvulsive therapy, an older client is expected to have:
questions.rationale: ECT commonly causes transient confusion and short-term memory loss, especially in older adults.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: ECT commonly causes short and long term memory loss and confusion, especially in geriatric clients. It rarely results in permanent

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: When assessing a victim of domestic violence, the most important information is her:
questions.rationale: Assess safety, readiness to leave and awareness of resources so options are available when she is ready.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: Victims of domestic violence must be assessed for thetr readiness to leave the perpetrator and their knov,ledge of the resources available to them.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client in group therapy is dramatic, seductive and seeks constant attention. These traits suggest:
questions.rationale: Histrionic PD: excessive emotionality and attention seeking, discomfort when not the center of attention.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 207)
questions.quote: lhe patient's behaviors are typical of histrionic personalit> disorder. "hich is marked by excessive emotionality and attention seeking.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client on lithium should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Adequate fluids and steady sodium intake prevent toxicity; avoid caffeine; continue the drug.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 207)
questions.quote: Patient's needs to maintain adequate fluid intake to avoid lithium toxicity.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The care plan for a client with anorexia nervosa should include:
options: Supervising meals and an hour after
Restricting family visits until she eats
questions.rationale: A strict eating plan with supervision during and after meals prevents hiding food or purging; involve the family.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 207)
questions.quote: Set up a strict eating plan, providing initially a one-on-one supervision dunng meals and for I hour afterward.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client with OCD brushes his forehead so often that the skin is irritated. The highest priority is to:
options: Set limits on the harmful ritual
Explore the meaning of the ritual
questions.rationale: Safety comes first; limit rituals that cause harm while teaching new ways to manage anxiety.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 207)
questions.quote: setting consistent limits on potentially harmful rituahstic tx•havior takes highest priority.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A long-term goal for a client with obsessive-compulsive rituals is to:
questions.rationale: Treatment systematically reduces ritual time and repetitions; stopping abruptly raises anxiety.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 210)
questions.quote: Systematically decrease the amount of time spent in- and the number of repeutions of rituals.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client says, "We can, pan, scan, ran, plan." This speech pattern is:
questions.rationale: Clang associations link words by sound (rhyme) rather than meaning.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 208)
questions.quote: Words that rhyme or sound alike. used in an illogical. nonsensical manner reflect clang association.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Which drug is prescribed to improve cognitive function in Alzheimer's disease?
questions.rationale: Donepezil is a cholinesterase inhibitor that improves cognition; antipsychotics treat agitation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 208)
questions.quote: Aricept is an anticholinesterase agent used to Improve cogruttse functioning in patients with Alzheimer's disease.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client taking disulfiram drinks alcohol. The nurse expects:
questions.rationale: The disulfiram-alcohol reaction causes flushing, headache, nausea, vomiting, chest pain, tachycardia and hypotension.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 209)
questions.quote: chest pain, shortness o breath, nausea, vomiting. facial flushing, headache, red eyes, blurred vision, sweating. tachycardia. hypotension

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A depressed client says, "Life isn't worth living." The nurse's best response is:
questions.rationale: Ask directly about suicidal thoughts to assess risk; asking does not plant the idea.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 209)
questions.quote: the nurse should begin a suicidal assessment with a direct question about suicide.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client in a manic episode is loud, provocative and shows poor judgment. The first priority is to:
questions.rationale: Mania involves overstimulation and impulsivity; reduce stimuli and protect from harm. Lithium is oral only.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 209)
questions.quote: The nurse should provide a safe, non- stimulating environment.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A 50-year-old with paranoid schizophrenia has never had a close friend and believes others plot against him. He has failed the developmental task of:
questions.rationale: Paranoid ideation reflects basic difficulty in trusting others.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 210)
questions.quote: Ihis patient's paranoid ideation indicates difficulty in trusting others.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which behavior would the nurse expect in a child with ADHD?
questions.rationale: ADHD causes impulsivity (blurting out answers), inattention, disorganization and hyperactivity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 1 (2024), Psychiatric exercises (PDF p. 208)
questions.quote: The child with ADHD typically has difficulty orgamzing tasks and following through with instructions due to problems Involving inattention
